title: Declarative agents: what Copilot runs for you, what it needs and where to stop it
summary: Hold: the page says User access has no documented automation, but Microsoft documents a preview Graph route that applies this setting. It also overstates what an untouched tenant permits and asserts that declarative agents have no price of their own without supporting text.

claims.claim: A declarative agent is defined by purpose, instructions, knowledge and actions.
claims.quote: You define the agent's purpose, instructions, knowledge, and supported actions to address a business scenario.

claims.claim: Declarative agents run on Copilot's orchestrator and models.
claims.quote: Declarative agents run on Microsoft 365 Copilot's managed orchestration and language-model infrastructure.

claims.claim: The managed declarative-agent runtime requires no hosting of its own.
claims.quote: Use Copilot's orchestrator and foundation model. No additional hosting is required.

claims.claim: The configuration describes agent identity and behaviour.
claims.quote: Identity and behavior: The agent's name, purpose, instructions, conversation starters, constraints, and visual representation.

claims.claim: Configured knowledge sources ground the agent's responses.
claims.quote: Knowledge: The approved information sources that ground responses.

claims.claim: Agent capabilities can include actions, skills, connectors and MCP-based tools.
claims.quote: Actions, skills, connectors, or MCP-based capabilities selected for the scenario.

claims.claim: Host and distribution metadata places the agent in supported Microsoft experiences.
claims.quote: Host and distribution metadata: The information required to surface the agent in supported Microsoft experiences.

claims.claim: Teams messages can supply declarative-agent knowledge.
claims.quote: Custom knowledge to connect Microsoft 365 data sources (such as Teams messages, Copilot connectors, SharePoint, and OneDrive)

claims.claim: Copilot connectors can supply declarative-agent knowledge.
claims.quote: Custom knowledge to connect Microsoft 365 data sources (such as Teams messages, Copilot connectors, SharePoint, and OneDrive)

claims.claim: SharePoint can supply declarative-agent knowledge.
claims.quote: Custom knowledge to connect Microsoft 365 data sources (such as Teams messages, Copilot connectors, SharePoint, and OneDrive)

claims.claim: OneDrive can supply declarative-agent knowledge.
claims.quote: Custom knowledge to connect Microsoft 365 data sources (such as Teams messages, Copilot connectors, SharePoint, and OneDrive)

claims.claim: Declarative agents run in Microsoft 365 Copilot and apps such as Teams, Word, Excel and Outlook.
claims.quote: Run in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 apps like Teams, Word, Excel, and Outlook.

claims.claim: Agent Builder is a low-code route for declarative agents.
claims.quote: Can be developed with low-code tools (Agent Builder) or Work IQ Dev Tools, the recommended tool for supported pro-code scenarios.

claims.claim: Agent Builder does not author external-service actions.
claims.quote: Agent Builder doesn't support authoring actions that integrate external services.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio can be used to build declarative agents.
claims.quote: Build a declarative agent when: ... You want a faster implementation or want to develop an agent with no or low-code using tools like Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Work IQ Dev Tools supports pro-code declarative-agent scenarios.
claims.quote: Work IQ Dev Tools is the recommended pro-code starting point for supported declarative-agent scenarios.

claims.claim: External integrations can still need code and hosting.
claims.quote: External integrations can still require code and hosting.

claims.claim: Custom engine agents use the maker's own orchestrator and models.
claims.quote: the custom engine approach, where you bring your own orchestrator and models to create a fully tailored agent.

claims.claim: Custom engine agents require hosting outside Microsoft 365, typically Azure, at additional cost.
claims.quote: Require additional hosting outside of Microsoft 365, typically with cloud services such as Azure, at an additional cost.
claims.fix: Replace the custom-engine Hosting cell with 'Hosted in Microsoft 365 with Copilot Studio or externally with custom solutions such as Azure AI', as the same page's Engine hosting comparison states.

claims.claim: Declarative agents do not support proactive interactions and rely on user initiation.
claims.quote: Proactive interactions | Not supported; rely on user-initiated interactions.

claims.claim: Custom engine agents can trigger actions without direct user input.
claims.quote: Enable agents to trigger actions automatically, even without direct user input.

claims.where: What it is: comparison table; Why it matters
claims.claim: Declarative agents inherit Microsoft 365 security, compliance and RAI requirements.
claims.quote: Because declarative agents use Copilot's AI infrastructure, model, and orchestrator, they adhere to the security, compliance, and Responsible AI (RAI) requirements for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Custom engine agent makers must ensure their own compliance and security.
claims.quote: Must ensure your own compliance, RAI practices, and security measures.

claims.where: Why it matters; What to check
claims.claim: Copilot uses existing permissions, so SharePoint grounding retains the user's existing reach.
claims.quote: Copilot uses existing permissions and policies to deliver the most relevant information, building on our existing commitments to data security and data privacy in the enterprise.

claims.claim: User access defaults to All users, subject to existing app policies and user assignments.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. It means that all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.

claims.claim: A tenant that never visits Agents has agents open to everyone with nobody deciding blocking, installation or group limits.
claims.quote: all users in the organization can access agents and plugins, subject to the existing app policies and user assignments.
claims.fix: Remove the final sentence beginning 'A tenant that never visits'. Retain the preceding qualified default statement; not visiting this portal does not establish the absence of existing app policies or user assignments.

claims.claim: A declarative agent has no price of its own.
claims.quote: Searched: declarative agents cost price separate agent charge Copilot Credits billing rates; declarative agents "no" "cost" "price". Read prerequisites, Agent Builder licensing, cost-considerations and billing-rate search excerpts; none states this blanket exemption.
claims.fix: Delete 'A declarative agent has no price of its own;' and start the paragraph 'What each user can do with a declarative agent depends on their licence or the tenant's billing.'

claims.quote: Have both a Microsoft 365 subscription and the Copilot add-on license (including Microsoft 365 Copilot Business and the E7 Frontier Suite, where applicable).

claims.claim: Usage-based billing enables agent access without a full licence.
claims.quote: Tenants can enable agent access without a full license, with some limitations to agent configuration options.

claims.claim: Usage-based consumption is measured in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Consumption is measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risks and limits
claims.claim: Users must meet the requirements of every capability an agent uses to access it.
claims.quote: Users can access a declarative agent only if they meet the requirements for all capabilities it uses.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; What to check
claims.claim: SharePoint-grounded agents under pay-as-you-go need a billing policy connected to the SharePoint agents service.
claims.quote: For agents that use SharePoint files as knowledge sources, the billing policy must be connected to the SharePoint agents service and users must be in the security group assigned to the billing policy.

claims.claim: Agent Builder agents do not consume the tenant's Dataverse storage entitlement.
claims.quote: Agents you build in Agent Builder don't consume the tenant's Dataverse storage entitlement.

claims.claim: The Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: Microsoft's Copilot Studio billing rates page holds usage billing rates.
claims.quote: For information about usage billing rates, see Billing rates and management.

claims.claim: Administrative actions apply to the selected agent, not necessarily its entire plugin package or tools.
claims.quote: These actions apply to the selected agent. If the agent is included in a plugin, don't assume the action also applies to the whole plugin package, its skills, shared MCP servers, or connections.

claims.claim: Blocking an agent does not necessarily revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.
claims.quote: Agent approval or blocking doesn't necessarily grant or revoke connected-service permissions or credentials.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Blocking acts on the agent only
claims.claim: Agents > Tools is the management route for plugins, skills and MCP servers.
claims.quote: To manage plugins, skills, and MCP servers, use Agents > Tools.

claims.claim: Blocking Agent Builder or Copilot Studio agents affects Copilot and other hosts.
claims.quote: It also affects availability and functionality in other host products, such as Microsoft Outlook, Microsoft Teams, or other Microsoft 365 applications.

claims.claim: Blocking SharePoint or Foundry agents affects only Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: However, blocking an agent that you created by using SharePoint or Microsoft Foundry only impacts its availability in Microsoft Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Administrators cannot disable Agent Builder creation separately while keeping agents enabled.
claims.quote: Administrators can't disable agent creation in Agent Builder separately while keeping agents enabled.

claims.claim: Administrators can control agent access, organisation-wide sharing and catalogue publishing approval.
claims.quote: They can control agent access, org-wide sharing, and approval for catalog publishing.

claims.claim: Instructions are not a deterministic workflow engine.
claims.quote: Evaluate representative tasks instead of treating instructions as a deterministic workflow engine.

claims.claim: Platform and model updates can change agent behaviour.
claims.quote: Platform and model updates can change behavior.

claims.claim: Large sources do not guarantee complete coverage in a response.
claims.quote: Large sources or payloads don't guarantee complete coverage in a response.

claims.claim: Scoped web search uses Bing-indexed content, which can be incomplete or stale.
claims.quote: Scoped web search uses Bing-indexed content rather than directly querying the underlying data source. Dynamically generated content can be incomplete or stale.

claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot takes precedence over Agent Builder's Web content toggle.
claims.quote: The Allow web search in Copilot policy takes precedence over the UI setting.

claims.claim: Agent Builder agents cannot be used in Teams group or 1:1 chats.
claims.quote: You can't use agents built in Agent Builder in Teams group or 1:1 chats.

claims.claim: Customer Managed Keys are not supported for Agent Builder agents.
claims.quote: Customer Managed Keys aren't supported for agents built in Agent Builder.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Government clouds differ
claims.claim: DoD supports only pro-code declarative agents.
claims.quote: Department of Defense (DoD): Limited support - only pro-code agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit are supported. Agent Builder isn't available for declarative agents in DoD.

claims.fix: Set controls[1].api to graph 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors', docs https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/configurationmanagement-post-configurationmonitors?view=graph-rest-beta. Replace its TCM note with 'Preview; mode=applyOnce applies baseline resources. For microsoft.agent.useraccess (resourceVersion 1), properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory sets everyone or noOne. Requires delegated permissions and AI Administrator for the signed-in user; TCM is global-service only.' In Open questions replace the API-gap bullet with 'Preview TCM applyOnce documents automation for User access, Agent and plugin access and Sharing; the useraccess schema documents everyone and noOne, not specific users or groups.' Use https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources and https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-remediation-applyonce-resources for the resource properties and role.
